pm_structure.summary: Outsourced model: the board Investment Committee (directors, officers and external experts) sets the investment policy, selects external investment managers within its authority (board approves larger mandates), reviews manager performance quarterly and monitors asset-liability matching. Manager names are not disclosed. Private-market exposure is via funds (real estate, infrastructure, private debt).
manager_entities: External managers (unnamed) selected by the Investment Committee
bullets: Investment Committee recommends investment policy to Board; quarterly review of policy, manager reports and ALM matching
Committee also oversees LS Travel's portfolio; external expert member (Michel Pelletier) sits on it
Single internal VP Investment & Special Projects (Luc Bergeron, FCIA FSA) in 2025 AR; no in-house trading desk disclosed
Alternatives held through funds: real estate C$19.6mm, infrastructure C$14.3mm, private debt C$3.2mm (first allocation 2025)
Cash-flow hedge accounting used (derivative assets C$0.1mm, liabilities C$0.1mm; OCI hedge reserve movements)

rotation_commentary.text: Data, not narrative: public shares fell from C$29.8mm to C$0.5mm while bonds rose C$5.7mm and a first C$3.2mm private-debt fund allocation appeared (AR balance sheet).
Net investment result fell to C$5.4mm from C$19.0mm (fair-value change -C$6.8mm); no management commentary on the drivers or on target mix.
Strategy narrative is operational (2025-2027 plan: digital transformation, IWME product line, travel embedded insurance); no asset-allocation targets published.

repos.text: Not disclosed; no repo line on the summary balance sheet.

structured_indirect.text: Fund-based alternatives: real estate funds C$19.6mm, infrastructure funds C$14.3mm, private debt funds C$3.2mm; loans C$27.2mm (type not disclosed).

leverage.note: No senior/sub debt, preferred shares or LRCNs. Lease liabilities C$0.5mm.

deals.text: Launched Oneday simplified-issue life brand; enhanced Emma (Quebec insurtech) life product; supported launch of Amoré AI life platform with EXOS Wealth Systems and Acceptiv.
Travel insurance embedded-distribution strategy: coverage built into partners' booking platforms; cruise-specific product.
Earlier strategic moves cited at Peliel's appointment: launch of L2A, alliance with Emma, acquisition of Tour+Med (travel; now LS Travel/Humania Travel Insurance).
Sold MGA Aurrea Signature to IDC Worldsource.
LS Mutual Life Insurance Company renamed Humania Assurance Inc.; parent LS Mutual Management kept mutual ownership while allowing share capital.

Bios (joined/industry start) for Bergeron, Dudau and Georgoulas not found; search budget exhausted before French-press lookups (Journal de l'assurance, Les Affaires).
notes: Humania is a C$0.65bn-asset Saint-Hyacinthe mutual (reported through its parent LS Mutual Management) with a C$0.41bn general account that is 78% bonds, outsourced to unnamed external managers under a board Investment Committee that includes an external expert. The book is heavily reinsured (reinsurance assets = 32% of total assets) and unlevered, with CARLI at 184%. 2025 saw public equities sold down to near zero and a first private-debt fund allocation, but management offers no rotation narrative. Its former CEO Marc Peliel is now CFO of Securian Canada. Personal library not available in this session; public sources used.
